exercises.prompt: Productiveness, in this unit, is which policy?

choices.text: Create the values your life needs
Wait for values to appear
Take what other people have made
Wish harder until the work is done

feedback.note: Productiveness is the virtue of making values by thought and effort.

exercises.prompt: Pride, in this unit, means what?

choices.text: Moral ambition: earn the right to respect yourself
Vanity: demand that others admire you
A title you inherit
Boasting with nothing behind it

feedback.note: Pride here is earned self-respect, not a claim on an audience.

exercises.prompt: Match each idea to the virtue or the opposite.

pairs.left: Become worthy of the life you are making
Live off values you did not earn

feedback.note: Productiveness supplies values. Pride is the character that has earned them. Taking is neither.

exercises.prompt: Build the link between the two virtues.

feedback.note: Productiveness is the making. Pride is the self-respect that making, and the rest of the code, can earn.

exercises.prompt: Which is pride, rather than vanity?

choices.text: Building a character you can honestly respect
Needing strangers to clap
Resting on a family name
Declaring that no standard applies to you

feedback.note: Pride looks at whether you have earned your own respect. Vanity looks at an audience.

choices.text: The world, by thought and effort, toward human needs
The facts, so work is unnecessary
Other people, so they must provide
Nothing; nature owes the values

feedback.note: Productiveness reshapes materials and plans. It does not pretend the facts will do the work.

exercises.prompt: Match the result to the virtue that aims at it.

pairs.left: Values brought into existence by work
A self you have made worth esteeming
A wish with no effort and no standard

feedback.note: Work without a moral standard is not yet pride. Self-regard without making or earning is not productiveness.

feedback.note: Making values is productiveness. Pride is the further demand that you become worthy of that life and earn your own respect.

exercises.prompt: Which pairing connects making values with moral ambition?

choices.text: Create what your life needs, and hold yourself to a character worthy of that life
Create what your life needs, then demand that strangers admire the result
Wait for values to appear, and inherit the right to respect yourself
Live off what others made, and call the taking self-respect

feedback.note: Productiveness is the making. Pride is the ambition to be worthy of the life you are making, not applause, inheritance, or unearned taking.
